s: a self-service bohemian bar with a hidden courtyard, right in Kazimierz
w: A self-service bar on Józefa street that captures Kazimierz's slightly raw, bohemian character better than most -- order coffee, wine or beer at the counter, then find a seat in the hidden courtyard garden out back when the weather allows. Unfussy and full of character rather than styled for visitors.
_facts: Located at ul. Józefa 9, 31-056 Kraków, Kazimierz
Self-service bar serving coffee, wine and beer
Has a courtyard garden seating area

s: a literary café where every coffee arrives with a printed quote
w: A used-book-lined café on Miodowa where quotes stencilled across the walls carry over into the cups -- every large coffee comes with its own printed quote to keep. A wall of board games and a quiet, unhurried pace round out one of Kazimierz's more bookish corners.
_facts: Located at ul. Miodowa 23/1, Kazimierz, Kraków
Literary-themed café with used books (mostly Polish) and quotes stencilled on the walls
Every coffee is served with a printed literary quote
Also stocks a wall of board games

s: a wobbly-furnitured Kazimierz institution with old photos of Kraków's Jewish community
w: One of Kazimierz's most atmospheric spots, its slightly wobbly furniture and pre-war photographs of Kraków's Jewish community hanging askew on the walls. Doubles as one of the neighbourhood's best-loved beer gardens, right by streets that once stood in for the Kraków ghetto in Schindler's List.
_facts: Located at ul. Meiselsa 20, 31-058 Kraków, Kazimierz
Known for pre-war-style decor, including old photographs of Kraków's Jewish community
Has a popular beer garden
Near filming locations used for Schindler's List

s: an old Kazimierz house with a hidden courtyard and its own screening room
w: A long-running Kazimierz restaurant on Józefa street, its interior spreading through an old townhouse into a quiet inner courtyard and a side room used for film screenings. International menu, relaxed pace, and the kind of layered, slightly worn interior that only comes from years in the same building.
_facts: Located at ul. Józefa 17, 31-056 Kraków, Kazimierz
Restaurant with an inner courtyard and a separate room used for film screenings
Serves an international menu

s: a café built into a Brutalist contemporary art gallery by the Planty
w: A café attached to Bunkier Sztuki, Kraków's contemporary art gallery, its striking modern architecture standing out against the Planty park greenery around Plac Szczepański. Coffee and food served in a space that belongs as much to the gallery's exhibitions as to its own café identity.
_facts: Located at Plac Szczepański 3a, Kraków, attached to the Bunkier Sztuki contemporary art gallery
Sits beside the Planty park ring around Kraków's Old Town
Shares its building with a rotating contemporary art exhibition space

s: an independent English-language bookshop and café near Wawel
w: An independent English-language bookshop spread through a warren of rooms on Felicjanek street, with a café tucked among the new and secondhand stacks. A short walk from Wawel Castle but resolutely bookish rather than touristy -- readings, a genuine local following, and the unhurried pace of a proper bookshop café.
_facts: Located at ul. Felicjanek 4, Kraków, a short walk from Wawel Castle
Independent English-language bookstore selling new and secondhand books
Has an attached café and hosts literary events/readings

s: a design-forward specialty café known for its animal-shaped desserts
w: A newer specialty coffee shop on Długa street pairing careful brews with a case of tiny, deliberately adorable desserts -- animal-shaped mono-portions alongside matcha and a small selection of Ukrainian-brand gifts. A considered, design-led addition to Kraków's Old Town-adjacent coffee scene.
_facts: Located at ul. Długa 24, 31-146 Kraków
Specialty coffee café known for animal-shaped dessert mono-portions
Also functions in part as a concept store for Ukrainian-made gifts and goods

s: a dedicated matcha bar with a design-forward interior in Podgórze
w: A café built entirely around matcha -- lattes, desserts and specialty drinks -- rather than treating it as a menu afterthought, in a considered, design-led space on the Podgórze side of the river. Part of the newer wave of single-focus specialty drink bars spreading beyond Kraków's Old Town and Kazimierz core.
_facts: Located at ul. Węgierska 12, Stare Podgórze, Kraków
Café focused specifically on matcha drinks and desserts
Closed Mondays

s: an Italian trattoria tucked down a passage off the Main Square
w: An Italian pizzeria and trattoria tucked into Pasaż Bielaka, a narrow passage just off Kraków's Main Square -- easy to miss unless you already know to duck in. Straightforward pizza and pasta in a small, characterful room a few steps from the square's much busier restaurants.
_facts: Located at Pasaż Bielaka 10, 31-042 Kraków, just off the Main Square
Italian restaurant (pizzeria/trattoria)
Tucked into a narrow pedestrian passage rather than facing the square directly

s: Kazimierz's round market hall, ringed by zapiekanka stalls
w: The small, circular market hall (the "okrąglak") at the centre of Kazimierz, built in the 1900s as a kosher poultry slaughterhouse and now ringed by stalls serving Kraków's favourite late-night snack -- open-faced zapiekanka, toasted with cheese and mushrooms and whatever else the stall owner insists on. Bars and cafés fill the surrounding square day and night.
_facts: Located at Plac Nowy, Kazimierz, Kraków
Central round market building ("okrąglak") originally built as a kosher poultry slaughterhouse
Surrounding stalls are known citywide for zapiekanka (open-faced toasted baguette)
Square is also lined with bars and cafés
